metadata.title: Simple critical zeros in short intervals: stability, parity, localization, Hilbert compression, and spectral defect
metadata.description:
For a conjugation-invariant finite multiset, let N count copies, S simple real support, O distinct odd-multiplicity real support, Q the squared-kernel pair sum, and D(G)=tr Psi_2(G) the retained simple-real Gram spectral defect. The paper proves the finite inequality (Q-S-D(G))(N-O) >= 2(N-S)^2 by coupling an attributed rank-trace theorem to odd support.

Combined with Wang's short-interval pair theorem and a localized rank-three Selberg detector, this yields a coupled quadratic lower bound for the lower asymptotic proportion of simple critical zeros. It strictly improves the complete positive EXP-006 curve. At theta=0.5459, directed rational arithmetic certifies H-h3 > 1.3732525985593292701164661575215e-70. The positivity onset remains in (0.545884,0.545885); the new spectral term does not lower it.

The product coefficient two is sharp. An analytic construction proves strict improvement wherever h3(theta)>0, and exact enumeration plus independent high-precision interval checks certify the finite and numerical components. The result is asymptotic and depends on recent attributed preprints. No effective starting height, global zero-density record, external peer review, or proof of the Riemann hypothesis is claimed. Source code, data, and computational records are available at https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH.
metadata.version_notes: Adds the spectral-defect parity product (Q-S-D(G))(N-O) >= 2(N-S)^2, an arbitrary-parameter finite proof, and its coupled short-interval transfer. The new root strictly improves the complete positive v0.06 curve, with an exact gain certificate at theta=0.5459, while leaving the positivity onset in (0.545884,0.545885). Adds EXP-007 exact enumeration and independent high-precision interval evidence, and evaluates post-cutoff Dirichlet-polynomial and projected-ordinate approaches. The Riemann hypothesis remains open.
